mainTopic: Meat versus liver in our משנה, how broadly food words reach in נדרים, and whether an agent who adds to his mission is still an agent
overview: Our משנה says that a שליח who serves liver when told to serve meat, or the reverse, has gone against his instructions. The גמרא asks which תנא holds that items an agent would ask about first count as two separate things. רב חסדא says this is not רבי עקיבא, who in נדרים forbids gourds to someone who vowed off vegetables. אביי answers that even רבי עקיבא agrees the שליח had to ask first, and רבא praises this. The גמרא then names רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as the one who reads food words narrowly: for him, liver and birds are not 'meat.' Next it asks why the first תנא counts birds as meat but not fish. רב פפא first places the case on a day of bloodletting, but birds are also avoided then, so he switches to a day of sore eyes, when only fish is avoided. Finally the גמרא tries to learn from the משנה that an agent who adds to his mission is still an agent. רב ששת rejects this proof: the agent may have split the order into one piece for the owner and one for himself.

steps.title: Who holds that items an agent would ask about are two separate things?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind our משנה's idea that meat and liver count as two different items.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who holds that any item a שליח would ask about before switching to it counts as a separate item?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking who the author of our משנה is. The משנה treated a שליח who swapped meat for liver as having broken his instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח would normally check with the owner before swapping meat for liver. The משנה treats such items as two different things, so the swap counts as going against instructions. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period whose teaching is being identified
An agent sent to act for someone else
That he would consult or ask permission

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who is the tanna
that any item about which an agent would consult
they are two separate items?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּכׇל מִילְּתָא דְּמִימְּלַךְ עֲלַהּ שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that items needing the owner's approval to swap count as two separate items

steps.title: רב חסדא says this does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא, who forbids gourds to someone who vowed off vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It does not follow רבי עקיבא. We learned: Someone who vows off vegetables may eat gourds, but רבי עקיבא forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by naming whose view the משנה does NOT follow. He backs this up with a משנה from נדרים about gourds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא counts gourds as part of 'vegetables,' since a שליח sent for vegetables would ask before buying gourds instead. To him, an item you would ask about belongs to the same category. Our משנה treats such items as two separate things, so רב חסדא says it cannot be רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow (נדר) forbidding something to himself

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
as we learned: One who vows off vegetables
is permitted to eat gourds,
but Rabbi Akiva forbids them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is not like רבי עקיבא, who counts gourds within 'vegetables'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In נדרים, תנא קמא permits gourds to one who vowed off vegetables, and רבי עקיבא forbids them

steps.title: אביי says even רבי עקיבא agrees the agent had to ask
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that our משנה can fit רבי עקיבא too, because even he holds that the שליח must ask before switching.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it is רבי עקיבא. Doesn't he agree the שליח needs to ask first?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב חסדא's claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא may count meat and liver as one category for vows. Still, a שליח who swaps without asking has not done what he was sent to do. So the משנה's ruling comes from the agent failing to ask, not from meat and liver being two categories.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...? (a question that expects 'yes')

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying that רבי עקיבא treats meat and liver as two categories. He is saying the משנה's ruling rests on a different reason: the agent failed to ask.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You may even say it is Rabbi Akiva,
doesn't he need to consult?
phrases.notes: He means the agent: even רבי עקיבא agrees the agent should have asked the owner before swapping.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חסדא assumed the ruling depends on meat and liver being two categories. It actually depends on the agent's duty to ask, which רבי עקיבא also accepts.

steps.title: רבא approves אביי's answer
steps.stepSummary: When אביי's answer was reported to רבא, he said אביי was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Rabbis said this before רבא, he said to them: נחמני is speaking well!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his stamp of approval to אביי's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's praise makes אביי's view the accepted one. Our משנה can follow רבי עקיבא too, since its ruling rests on the agent's failure to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: He is speaking well; he is right

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, accepted by רבא, the agent is liable because he swapped without asking. This works even for רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: When the Rabbis said this before Rava,
he said to them: Nachmani is saying well!
phrases.notes: נחמני is a name רבא uses for אביי.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's approach stands: the משנה can follow even רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא disagrees with רבי עקיבא's broad reading of food categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question, which sets up the next step. It wants to know who holds the opposite of רבי עקיבא's view in the gourd debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נדרים, the first opinion was stated without a name. The גמרא now wants to identify who that unnamed sage is.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: Who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the נדרים debate raised by רב חסדא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who rejects רבי עקיבא's broad view of categories

steps.title: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who permits liver after a vow on meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. In a ברייתא about a vow on meat, he permits the head, feet, liver and birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as we learned in a ברייתא: Someone who vows off meat is forbidden all kinds of meat. He is also forbidden the head, feet, windpipe, liver and heart, and bird meat. He is permitted fish and grasshoppers. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits the head, feet, windpipe and liver, and birds, fish and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as the one who disagrees with רבי עקיבא. It proves this with a ברייתא about vowing off meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא reads 'meat' broadly, including organs and birds. That is like רבי עקיבא, who includes gourds in 'vegetables.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads 'meat' narrowly and leaves out parts like liver, so he matches the opinion that disagrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא reads food words broadly. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads them narrowly; for him, liver is not 'meat.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties our משנה's meat-versus-liver case back to the debate in נדרים over how broad a food word is.

phrases.english: It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
as it is taught: One who vows off meat
is forbidden all kinds of meat,
and is forbidden the head and the feet,
the windpipe, the liver, and the heart.
And he is forbidden the meat of birds,
but is permitted the meat of fish and grasshoppers.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits
the head and the feet, the windpipe and the liver,
and birds, fish, and grasshoppers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who reads 'meat' narrowly
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one who vows off meat
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא forbids organs and birds to one who vowed off meat. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits them.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: innards are not meat
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that innards are not considered meat, and people do not normally eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used to say: innards are not meat, and whoever eats them is not a normal person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It shows how narrowly he defines 'meat'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל left the head, feet, liver and birds out of 'meat'. Here he goes further and says innards are not even normal food. This confirms that he is the תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא's broad reading of food categories.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And likewise Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say:
Innards are not meat,
and one who eats them is not a person.
phrases.notes: He means innards are not something people normally eat, so they don't count as 'meat'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that supports the identification made in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל defines 'meat' narrowly
steps.raayaSupportSource: His statement that innards are not meat

steps.title: Why does the first תנא count birds as meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first תנא of the ברייתא includes birds in a vow on meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the first תנא, what is special about bird meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the first תנא of the ברייתא. It asks for his reason for treating birds as meat. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds are a different kind of creature from animals. So why should a vow on 'meat' cover them? The גמרא wants to know what makes birds fit into the meat category for the first תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And according to the first Tanna,
what is different about meat of birds?
phrases.notes: Unlike רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first תנא forbids birds to someone who vowed off meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא, מַאי שְׁנָא בִּבְשַׂר עוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view to the reasoning of the first תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the first תנא includes birds in a vow on meat

steps.title: People speak of bird as a substitute for meat
steps.stepSummary: Birds count as meat because people commonly say they brought bird when they couldn't find animal meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people commonly say: 'I didn't find animal meat, so I brought bird meat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. In everyday speech, bird meat is treated as a stand-in for animal meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נדרים follow how people normally talk. Since people naturally swap bird meat for animal meat, bird falls under the word 'meat'.

keyTerms.meaning: A person is accustomed (to say or do)

phrases.english: Because a person commonly says:
I did not find meat of an animal,
so I brought meat of a bird.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Common speech treats bird meat as a replacement for animal meat

steps.title: People would say the same about fish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: people also say they brought fish instead of meat, so fish should count as meat too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a person would also say: 'I didn't find animal meat, so I brought fish!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 9. That reasoning should make fish count as meat as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא allows fish to someone who vowed off meat. But if 'people substitute it' is the test, fish also passes the test. So the reason given for birds seems to prove too much.

phrases.english: If so,
a person is also apt to say:
I did not find meat of an animal,
so I brought fish!
phrases.notes: So why does the first תנא let this person eat fish?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָכִי נָמֵי עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that birds count as meat because people substitute them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same substitution happens with fish, yet the first תנא does not count fish as meat

steps.title: רב פפא: the case is a day of bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the case is a day of bloodletting, when people don't eat fish, so fish would never be the substitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: we are talking about a day of bloodletting, when a person does not eat fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the first תנא. He limits the case to a day of bloodletting, when fish is not eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On such a day nobody would bring fish in place of meat. So the substitution argument works only for birds. That explains why fish is left out of 'meat'.

keyTerms.meaning: A day of bloodletting (a medical treatment)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We are dealing with a day of bloodletting,
when a person does not eat fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּיוֹם הַקָּזָה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fish should count as meat just like birds
steps.terutzMaskana: On a day of bloodletting fish is not eaten, so only birds are the natural substitute

steps.title: שמואל: birds are also harmful after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that on a day of bloodletting people would not eat birds either, as שמואל warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should not eat bird either, for שמואל said: whoever lets blood and eats bird, his heart flutters like a bird!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer. According to שמואל, bird is also dangerous after bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the day of bloodletting rules out fish, it should rule out birds too. Then birds would also not be a natural substitute. The first תנא's reason for including birds falls apart again.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, צִיפְּרָא נָמֵי לָא נֵיכוֹל,
phrases.english: If so, he should not eat bird either,
for Shmuel said:
one who has let blood and eats bird —
his heart flies like a bird!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, צִיפְּרָא נָמֵי לָא נֵיכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that on a day of bloodletting fish, but not birds, is avoided
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says bird is also harmful after bloodletting, so birds would not be a substitute either

steps.title: A ברייתא: no bloodletting before fish, birds or salted meat
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: a ברייתא says not to let blood before eating fish, birds or salted meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it is taught: one does not let blood before fish, nor before birds, nor before salted meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second source against רב פפא. A ברייתא groups birds together with fish as foods to avoid around bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a ברייתא, not only שמואל, treats birds exactly like fish. So the day of bloodletting cannot explain why the first תנא separates birds from fish. The challenge succeeds, and in the next step רב פפא drops this answer and gives a new one.
steps.whatToRemember: The first תנא counts birds as meat because people substitute bird for animal meat. רב פפא's attempt to explain why fish is different is challenged twice, by שמואל and by a ברייתא.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַקִּיזִין דָּם לֹא עַל הַדָּגִים,
phrases.english: One does not let blood, not before fish,
phrases.notes: 'Before' here means letting blood and then eating these foods on that day.

phrases.english: nor before birds,
nor before salted meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, ברייתא-based challenge on top of שמואל's statement in Step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists birds alongside fish as foods to avoid with bloodletting, so birds would not be substitutes either

steps.title: רב פפא's new case: a day when the eyes hurt
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא drops the bloodletting answer. He says the case is a day when the person's eyes hurt, and people do not eat fish then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: We are dealing with a day when his eyes hurt him, when a person does not eat fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The bloodletting answer was knocked down, so רב פפא offers a different day that fits better. On that day fish is avoided, but birds are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with bloodletting was that people avoid birds then too (steps 12-13). A day of sore eyes rules out fish only, so birds stay a natural replacement for meat. That again explains why birds count as 'meat' here and fish do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer and give a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: In this case fish is never a replacement for meat, because people with sore eyes avoid fish. Birds, though, are a normal replacement. So for the first תנא, a vow on 'meat' covers birds but not fish.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
We are dealing with a day that his eyes hurt him,
when he does not eat fish.
phrases.notes: Fish were thought to be bad for sore eyes, so nobody would bring fish that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the bloodletting case after it was challenged in steps 12-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so that it excludes fish but not birds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bloodletting day: but birds are also avoided then, so the answer failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A day of sore eyes: only fish is avoided, so bird remains the normal stand-in for meat.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה: an agent who adds is still an agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of 'give each guest one piece', where the agent said 'take two'. It learns that an agent who adds to his instructions is still counted as an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he said to him: Give him a piece, etc.' Learn from this: one who adds to his agency is still an agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. The owner said 'one piece each', the agent said 'take two', and the owner is still liable for מעילה. The גמרא tries to prove that adding to a mission does not cancel being an agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the sender is liable for מעילה only if the agent actually did the sender's mission. Here the agent went beyond the instructions, yet the owner is still liable. So it seems that adding to the mission still counts as carrying it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. The rest of the quote is left out
Adds to his mission, does more than he was told

steps.confusionAlert: The agent did not ignore the owner. He did what was asked and added more on top. The question is only about adding, not about doing something completely different.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: תֵּן לוֹ חֲתִיכָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: [The משנה says:] He said to him: Give him a piece, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: the agent told them 'take two', they took three, and everyone is liable.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
One who adds to his agency is still an agent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next case in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That an agent who adds to his mission is still considered the owner's agent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: owner said give one piece, agent said take two, and the owner is liable.

steps.title: רב ששת: the agent split the order into two separate parts
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the משנה may be a case where the agent said: 'take one piece for the owner and one for me.' So no proof comes from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The case is where the agent said: 'Take one piece by the owner's wishes and one by my own wishes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back the proof from step 15. He explains the משנה in a narrower way that teaches nothing about 'adding'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the agent clearly split it up, the first piece is exactly the owner's mission, so the owner is liable for it. The second piece is the agent's own separate act. So the משנה never mixed extra into the mission, and we cannot learn that one who adds is still an agent.

keyTerms.meaning: By his (the owner's) wishes or intent
By my (the agent's) own wishes or intent

steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves open whether an agent who adds to his mission is still an agent. The משנה is now read as two separate acts, not one larger act.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
[The case is] where the agent said:
Take one according to his intent
phrases.notes: 'His' means the owner who sent him.

phrases.english: and one according to my intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not say the opposite rule is true.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as two separate acts, one for the owner and one for the agent, so it says nothing about an agent who adds within one act.
